candidates.subject: Shield making, ceremonial deposition, and the ambiguity between weapon and prestige object

candidates.scan_source: Open-licensed institutional cultural-heritage 3D model via Sketchfab
candidates.note: A thin repoussé Yetholm shield with eleven concentric ribs and eleven rows of bosses; the museum's primary record treats it as a likely votive deposition and doubts that it was used in combat.
candidates.source_description: Culture: [Bronze Age](http://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p0ff3dtkhrj). Material: Bronze Diam. 63.8cm Accession No: HCA 457 Current Location: [The Hunt Museum](https://www.huntmuseum.com/), [Limerick](https://www.geonames.org/7778675/limerick-city.html). Circular, Yetholm type [shield](http://vocab.getty.edu/page/aat/300036869) of thin sheet-bronze, beaten to an even thickness of 0.5mm. Decorated with 11 concentric repoussé ribs and 11 rows of low hemispherical bosses with a hollow, rounded conical central boss. The rim is rolled over. Six tears and one perforation represent damage from the rear and front. It is unlikely that this object was ever used in combat. Yetholm shields have been found in England (15), Scotland (9), Wales (2) and Ireland (2). This one was recovered from the Thames at Halliford Upper, [Walton-on-Thames](https://www.geonames.org/2634825/walton-on-thames.html). [More](https://tinyurl.com/yyf5zhn5).
